column1: # The official suite's optional/format/json-pointer.json runs RFC 6901 §5's own
# examples, so those are not re-transcribed. Every §5 example is a valid
# pointer, though, which leaves the escape rule's rejecting side untested, and
# that rule is the whole of what this validator checks beyond the leading
# solidus: a '~' must be followed by '0' or '1'.
# Format: three tab-separated fields, "<input>"\t<valid>\t<note>. The input is a
# Go quoted string literal in the spelling strconv.Quote produces. '#' lines and

column3: the empty pointer names the whole document
~0 then a literal '1', which spells the member name ~1
%2F is an ordinary member-name character, not an escape
a non-empty pointer must begin with a solidus
an escape does not stand in for the leading solidus
a tilde at the end of a member name escapes nothing
